# feat: xRegistry-backed message listing and typed subscription scaffolding

**Home repo:** `intropy-cli` (this repository). The plan also touches two sibling
repos: `intropy-registry` (the xRegistry server, at `~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry`)
and the Intropy template library (fetched by `internal/template`). Paths below are
relative to the repo each unit names.

content.content:
## Implementation Notes

Recorded at execution time (2026-09-02); where these differ from the unit
text above, the notes are what shipped.

- **Registry fetch is lazy in effect, not just in scope.** The original
  design fetched the export up front whenever a template declared a
  message-ref parameter and failed the create on any fetch error.
  End-to-end verification with the real loader template showed this broke
  the manual topic/contract flow whenever the registry was down or
  unconfigured. As shipped: the fetch feeds only prompt suggestions, a
  fetch failure degrades to a stderr warning, and a hard error requires an
  actual message-ref value (commit `fix(template): require the registry
  only when a message reference is used`).
- **Injection conflict rule refined.** The plan said "a conflicting
  explicit value is an error". As shipped, only a conflicting `--set`
  errors; template defaults, `spec.values` derivations and values-file
  values yield to the registry with a stderr note. Motivation: the loader
  derives `pubsub: 'pubsub'` as a platform convention, and conventions
  must not conflict with the registry's fact about a specific message
  (commit `fix(template): let registry override derived wiring values`).
- **Contract suggestion timing.** The plan sketched the suggestion feeding
  the contract prompt. As shipped, the suggestion fills an unset contract
  post-resolution with a stderr note (same visibility regime as facts
  prefill); a contract the developer supplied always stands. Prompt-time
  suggestion would require registry access inside the prompt loop and is a
  possible follow-up.
- **Message name/description live on the default version** in real export
  documents (the server normalizes message-level attributes onto the
  version); `ResolvedMessage.DisplayName/DisplayDescription` hide the
  split. Found by live smoke against `task dev` in intropy-registry.
- **Live verification** (U1/U2/U5): `int message list`, `int message show`
  (plain and JSON, error paths) run against the real registry; the edited
  loader manifest was driven end-to-end through `Create` against the live
  registry (subscription flow resolves; legacy flow untouched; anyOf guard
  validates) via a throwaway test, since the library's `intropy.io/v1`
  apiVersion rename is ahead of this branch — the CLI-side rename rides
  the existing `chore/intropy-dev-to-io` branch.
- **U5 landed in intropy-templates** on branch `feat/loader-message-ref`
  (not pushed): the loader gains an optional `subscription` parameter,
  `topic`/`contract` leave `required`, and an `anyOf` guard keeps one of
  the two flows mandatory.

---

## U7 — Derived wiring parameters (message is the subscription)

Post-review refinement, agreed 2026-09-02: the message is the
subscription; the topic is routing the registry dictates. Parameters a
message-ref resolution expands (`topic`, `contract`) stop being things
the developer is asked for and become derived outputs — recorded
everywhere they are needed (Dapr wiring, scaffold record) but with
exactly one author, so a prefilled value can never fight a picked
message.

- [x] Manifest annotation `x-intropy-derived: true` →
      `FieldSpec.Derived`. Derived fields are never prompted
      (`missingRequired` skips them; schema validation stays the
      backstop), and an explicit `--set` still applies — the CLI escape
      hatch.
- [x] `template.PreviewWiring(export, messageID)` + per-message `wiring`
      previews on the dashboard detail response (`FieldSpec.Wiring`),
      filled by `suggestForDir` from the cached export.
- [x] Dashboard form: derived fields hidden and their seeded values
      stripped from the submission (`submitValues`) unless the user
      toggles "enter topic and contract manually"; a picked message shows
      its routing read-only under the control ("routes via
      pubsub/topic · contract Name (suggested)").
- [x] Loader manifest (intropy-templates, `feat/loader-message-ref`):
      `topic` and `contract` marked derived; the `anyOf` guard stays as
      the escape-hatch validation.

**Verification.** Go: manifest parse, never-prompted (validation
backstop), dashboard wiring preview tests. Live UI against the real
registry via a throwaway test server carrying the actual loader manifest
(temp workspace, derived fields hidden, wiring summary on pick, manual
toggle reveals and re-hides).

**Files.** `internal/template/{manifest,messageref,values}.go` (+tests),
`internal/dashboard/templates.go` (+test), `web/src/{api.ts,
components/{useTemplateFields.ts,form.tsx,CreateDrawer.tsx},index.css}`,
`intropy-templates/loader/template.yaml`.

---

## Sources & References

- Registry repo: `~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry` — README (shape, naming,
  compliance), `src/http/negotiate.ts` (Accept rules), `registry/` (sample
  data), `spec/` (vendored xRegistry models)
- CLI wiring vocabulary: `internal/template/wiring.go`
- Scaffold record: `internal/template/scaffold.go`
- System assembly consumer: `internal/system/blocks.go`
- xRegistry spec: https://xregistry.io (vendored under
  `intropy-registry/spec/`)

apiVersion: intropy.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: loader
  title: Loader Integration
  description: Long-running ASP.NET loader that subscribes to a Dapr pub/sub topic over HTTP delivery, runs each delivered message through the Intropy loader pipeline, and writes the result through a local destination folder binding.
  tags:
    - example
    - dotnet
    - dapr
    - loader
  labels:
    intropy.io/template-level: example
    intropy.io/block-kind: loader
    intropy.io/data-flow: "out"

spec:
  parameters:
    type: object
    required:
      - name
      - organization
    # The wiring comes from one of two sources: a message registry
    # reference (subscription), which the CLI expands into topic, pubsub
    # and a contract suggestion, or the topic and contract typed by hand.
    # The registry path is the primary one: topic and contract are marked
    # derived so prompts and forms leave them to the expansion, and the
    # manual path is an explicit opt-out (--set on the CLI, a toggle in
    # the dashboard) rather than an equal choice.
    anyOf:
      - required: [subscription]
      - required: [topic, contract]
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
        title: Project name
        description: PascalCase identifier used for the .NET project, root namespace, and assembly. Dot-separated segments are allowed for nested namespaces (e.g. OrderLoader or Int1055.OrderLoader).
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)*$"
      organization:
        type: string
        title: Organization
        description: PascalCase name of the organization the integration runs for. Becomes the telemetry ServiceNamespace and the business-incident source URN (urn:<organization>:<component>).
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$"
      subscription:
        type: string
        title: Message subscription
        description: Message to subscribe to, as a message id or xid from the Intropy message registry (int message list). When set, the CLI resolves the topic, pubsub component and a contract suggestion from the registry; leave empty to wire topic and contract by hand.
        x-intropy-message-ref: true
      topic:
        type: string
        title: Topic
        description: The pub/sub topic the loader subscribes to. This is the loader's half of the system contract — scaffold the publishing extractor with the same value. Filled from the registry when subscription is set; only set it by hand when subscribing to a topic the registry does not declare.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
        x-intropy-derived: true
      contract:
        type: string
        title: Contract type
        description: PascalCase name of the shared-contracts record the topic carries — the other half of the system contract, recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json for `intropy sys create` to type the topic with. The sample logic uses Order. Suggested from the message's schema when subscription is set.
        pattern: "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$"
        x-intropy-derived: true
      idempotencyAppId:
        type: string
        title: Idempotency service app-id
        description: Dapr app-id of the Idempotency Service. The default matches the platform-services deployment.
        default: "idempotency-service.services"
      businessIncidentsAppId:
        type: string
        title: Business incident service app-id
        description: Dapr app-id of the Business Incident Service. The default matches the platform-services deployment.
        default: "business-incident-service.services"
      empty:
        type: boolean
        title: Empty bodies
        description: When true, strip sample business logic from pipeline step bodies. The resulting project compiles and starts under Dapr, but every step throws NotImplementedException so a migration agent can fill them in. The idempotency and business-incident wiring stays (the loader pipeline requires it); idempotency keys off CloudEvent Subject/Time from the context, so there are no extractor lambdas to stub.
        default: true
  values:
    appId: '{{ .name | kebabcase | replace "." "-" }}'
    # The component's .NET project name, recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json
    # for workspace-level tooling (e.g. solution file assembly).
    projectName: '{{ .name }}'
    # Name of the sibling shared-contracts project; also drives the dependency
    # output below and the ProjectReference in the skeleton csproj. Plain
    # "Contracts" on purpose: the project is scoped to the system directory it
    # lives in, not to the organization.
    contracts: 'Contracts'
    # The pub/sub component name the skeleton subscribes through
    # (Constants.cs). Recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json for
    # `intropy sys create`, together with the contract parameter above.
    pubsub: 'pubsub'
    # The loader's destination port — the named interface it writes the
    # outside world through. Derived like appId so it stays unique per
    # component. Recorded in .intropy/scaffold.json; `intropy sys create`
    # resolves it to a local file transport by default (external system and
    # transport are never asked for at scaffold time).
    port: '{{ .name | kebabcase | replace "." "-" }}-destination'
  dependencies:
    - template: shared-contracts
      output: '{{ .contracts }}'
      values:
        name: '{{ .contracts }}'
        contract: '{{ .contract }}'
        empty: '{{ .empty }}'

---
# Writing style — comments, help text, and CLI output

This file is the house style for everything a reader sees: Go doc comments,
`--help` output, and the strings a command prints or returns as errors. It
applies to every Go file in this repository. Keep it short enough that it can
be re-read before every PR.

---

## Code comments

**Explain why, not what changed.** A comment answers the question the code
cannot: the invariant, the trade-off, the reason a non-obvious choice is the
safe one. It never narrates history.

- Never reference a PR, issue, fix, or the past tense of the code itself.
  "Used to", "now", "previously", "after the refactor", "fixes #123" are all
  forbidden. Git history already knows; the reader of the code does not care.
- A doc comment on every exported symbol. One or two sentences is usually
  enough. `golint` enforces this; don't make a reviewer do it.
- Target ≤ 10 lines per doc block. If you need more, the extra content
  belongs in `docs/` or a README, not above the function.
- "Deliberately not X" comments are encouraged when they stop a plausible
  wrong refactor. `internal/gitops/remote.go` is the exemplar: it says the
  function is *not* used to derive the cache directory, and why.
- No TODO, FIXME, HACK, or XXX in committed code. File an issue instead.

---

## Help text (cobra)

`--help` is reference material, not a blog post. A reader in a terminal wants
to know what the command does, what it costs, and which flags change the
behavior. Philosophy and motivation belong in `docs/`.

- **`Short:`** one line, imperative verb, no trailing period.
  Good: `Pin a component's image digest into an environment`
  Bad:  `This command pins the image digest.`
- **`Long:`** target ≤ 150 words, hard ceiling ~200. Cover: what it does,
  what it reads, what it writes, what can go wrong that the user can prevent.
  Cut: why the command exists, why GitOps is good, architecture essays.
- **`Use:`** positional args in `<>`, optional in `[]`, variadic as `name...`.
  Good: `pin <component> [version]`
  Bad:  `pin COMPONENT [VERSION]`, `pin <component> [<version>]`

If a `Long:` draft exceeds 200 words, the excess is almost always the second
paragraph onwards. Move it to a file under `docs/` and keep the help text
to usage.

---

## Flag descriptions

Use the shared constants in `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go`. Never hand-write a new
description for a flag another command already has:

- `--output`, `--env`, `--gitops-repo`, `--argocd-server`, `--domain`,
  `--system`, `--template-version` all have constants.
- If you add a flag that several commands will share, add a constant first.
- Flag descriptions are fragments, not sentences: no trailing period, no

content.content:
- Flag descriptions are fragments, not sentences: no trailing period, no
  "This flag…". Start with the noun. Good: `target environment (required)`.

---

## Runtime output

A CLI's output is read twice: once by a human scanning, once by a script
parsing. The two never share a stream.

- **stdout is for results.** Tables, JSON, the thing the command was run to
  produce.
- **stderr is for everything else.** Progress, warnings, completion messages,
  errors. A pipeline reading stdout must never see a status line.

### Voice

- Progress and completion: **lowercase, present tense, no trailing period**.
  Good: `syncing api on argocd.example.com at a1b2c3d`
  Good: `published ghcr.io/example/releases/api:1.2.0`
  Bad:  `Published ghcr.io/…`  `Sync complete.`
- Empty states follow the same rule: `no releases found`, not
  `No releases found.`
- A follow-up hint naming a command goes on its own line, in backticks:
  `use 'intropy release create <component>' to publish one`

### Errors

- Front-load what failed. The remediation, if there is one, goes on a second
  line. Do not editorialize — the user is already reading an error.
  Good: `pending change is a1b2c3d, not the f4e5d6c you reviewed`
        `run 'intropy deploy diff api --env staging' before syncing`
  Bad:  `…has advanced since you reviewed it — you really should read the new diff…`
- Wrap errors with context as they travel up: `fmt.Errorf("pull %s: %w", …)`.
  The outermost prefix names the command or operation, not the internals.

### Vocabulary

- **image digest**, not "bits", "artifacts", or "the images".
- **environment** in prose, `--env` only when naming the flag.
- `->` for a transition (`1.0 -> 1.1`), ` @ ` for a pin (`api @ 1.2.0`).
  Never mix the two in one message.
- A commit SHA is shown short (7 chars) unless the full value is the point.

### Command verbs

One verb per meaning, used on every noun (`int`, `template`, `deploy`, ...).
The full set, grouped by what the verb does to the world:

**Read-only** — exit 0 even when the answer is "they disagree", never write
to git, never trigger a sync:

- **`list`** enumerates a collection: integrations on disk, templates in the
  library, published releases. It never prints one item's
  details.
- **`show`** prints the details of exactly one thing: a template's manifest,
  an integration's scaffold record. It never enumerates.
- **`status`** reports one component across every environment, one row
  each, and whether the rows agree. It never prints one environment's
  details — that is `show`.
- **`diff`** prints the rendered change a `sync` would apply, as the
  resources themselves. Both sides are committed revisions; it never diffs
  an uncommitted worktree.
- **`inspect`** prints the deployment model derived from one system topology:
  components, workloads, ports, and available local fixtures. It never
  renders manifests or writes project or Git state.
- **`render`** emits a complete Kubernetes YAML stream for one environment.
  It may ask for missing local fixture choices, buffers and validates the whole
  stream before writing stdout, writes all interaction and diagnostics to
  stderr, and never changes project, Git, or cluster state.

**Create or change project state** — may write files under the project.
Manifest creation may push a review branch, never the default branch:

- **`create`** makes something new from a template or from scaffolded
  parts: an integration, a system host, a release manifest to publish, or
  missing Kubernetes manifests on a GitOps review branch. Manifest creation
  accepts existing identical files but never replaces or deletes a file.
- **`add`** attaches something that already exists elsewhere to this
  project: a library registration. Unlike
  `create`, the content is pulled, not generated.
- **`update`** reconciles something installed against the ref its source
  now pins: a cached index against the registry. It never changes which
  ref is pinned — that is the publisher's job.
**Move or publish** — change what runs somewhere or what others can pull:

- **`publish`** pushes an immutable artifact to an OCI registry: a release
  manifest. What is published cannot be edited in
  place; a new version is a new publish.
- **`pin`** writes one component's image digest into one environment's
  overlay.
- **`promote`** copies the digests one environment runs into the next
  environment in the promotion graph.
- **`sync`** applies an environment's pending change through ArgoCD. It
  never decides what the change is — that is `pin` and `promote`.
- **`use`** selects which named customer context subsequent commands act
  on. Neither `update` (reconciles an installed thing against its source)
  nor `pin` (writes one component's digest) covers selecting the operator's
  active context, and `use` is the name kubeconfig muscle memory expects
  for it. It never creates or edits contexts — those are authored in the
  config file by hand.

Do not import kubectl's `get`/`describe` split — `int describe` was retired
because it described templates, not integrations. New verbs need a reason
that the set above cannot express, and the reason goes in this file with
the verb, not in a commit message.

---

## What this file is not

It does not replace `CONTRIBUTING.md` (workflow, tests, commit convention) or
`README.md` (what the CLI is). When those disagree with this file, this file
wins on writing style and loses on everything else.

content.text:
Picked it up and finished it. Here's what was in flight and what I found.

**What was cut off:** the CLI counterpart of the dashboard's message dropdown. The dashboard side is committed (`2e0a7793`, `7d5efd7b`); the working tree had a half-finished `promptForMessageRefs` in `internal/template/values.go` plus an "Enter skips" affordance in the prompter. All plan units U1–U7 were already checked off, so this was an unrecorded follow-up.

**Why it was needed:** U7 marked `topic` and `contract` derived (never prompted) and left `subscription` optional, so an interactive `int create` on the loader asked for *nothing* and then failed schema validation.

**Four real gaps in the draft, now fixed:**

1. `internal/template/prompt.go:60` — a single-message catalog took the shown-default path, so Enter *accepted* the subscription instead of skipping. Optional fields now always render as a list, where Enter means skip.
2. With the registry down or unconfigured, the draft still prompted — a bare `subscription:` with no list, asking for a message id from memory that couldn't be resolved anyway. The catalog now travels as `ResolveOptions.MessageRefCandidates` and an empty one cancels the prompt. That also let me retire the `messageRefPrompter` wrapper: the list is a resolution input like `Facts`, not a prompter decoration.
3. Pressing Enter produced raw `jsonschema: '' does not validate with inline://params.json#/anyOf/0/required` text. A sole failed `anyOf` is now restated as `the template requires either subscription, or topic and contract`. A run that also violates a parameter's own pattern keeps the library's message, which names the parameter — pinned by a test.
4. An interactive create on a subscriber template with no registry configured got silence. `missingRegistryNote` now says so and names `--registry-url` / `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL` / `registryUrl`.

**Verified** against the real loader manifest at `~/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-templates/loader/template.yaml` (branch `feat/loader-message-ref`) driven through `ResolveWith` + `resolveMessageRefs` across all four paths — pick a message (topic/pubsub/contract all derived), skip, `--set` manual wiring (no prompt at all), registry absent. `make check` and `go vet ./...` pass; the throwaway probes are removed. Recorded as **U8** in the plan doc.

**Two commit points, and one caveat:** `make check` runs `gofmt -w`, which fixed pre-existing drift in `internal/system/payload.go` and `internal/template/facts.go` — unrelated to this work. I'd suggest a `style:` commit for those two files first, then the feature commit over `internal/template/{values,create,messageref,prompt}.go` (+tests) and the plan doc. Want me to make them?

# Customer contexts, kubeconfig-style: each context bundles the settings that
# change together when switching customer. Precedence is flag > environment >
# active context > the top-level keys below.
#
# The top-level keys mirror the entrovia context so that single-customer

content.text:
Your build is fine — the combobox is missing for two reasons, both outside the Go code, and I verified each.

## 1. The dashboard is serving a loader template that has no `subscription` parameter

GitHub's "latest release" for `intropy-templates` resolves to **v0.4.12**, and that manifest has no message-ref parameter at all — so there is no field for the frontend to turn into a dropdown:

```
$ ./bin/intropy template show loader
Loader Integration (loader) @ integrio-intropy/intropy-templates@v0.4.12
```

Where the manifest work actually lives:

| ref | `subscription` | `topic`/`contract` derived |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.4.12` — GitHub "latest release" | no | no |
| `v0.9.0` — newest cached tag | **yes** | no |
| `feat/loader-message-ref` — pushed, unmerged | yes | **yes** |

## 2. No registry is configured

Your `config.yaml` has no `registryUrl` and `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL` is unset. Without it `registryExport` returns nil, `registryMessageIDs` returns nil, and the field deliberately degrades to a plain text input (`internal/dashboard/templates.go:353`). The registry server itself *is* running on :8787 — `int message list` returns two messages.

## To see it right now

```
INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL=http://localhost:8787 intropy dashboard --template-version v0.9.0
```

I ran this against a scratch workspace and the API returns what the dropdown needs:

```
subscription   messageRef   suggestions=2   + per-message wiring previews
```

Caveat: v0.9.0 doesn't mark `topic`/`contract` as derived, so those two fields will still be visible. Full U7 behaviour needs `feat/loader-message-ref` merged and tagged.

## Two bugs found while diagnosing

**`--template-version <branch>` silently resolves to a different version.** `--template-version feat/loader-message-ref` reports `@v0.9.0`. The branch checkout never materializes (only `feat/loader-message-ref.lock` in the cache), and `FetchSource` falls back to the newest cached tag — I didn't determine why the clone fails. Related: `checkoutDir` treats the ref as immutable ("a tag's tree never changes, so existence is validity"), so a branch would never refresh even on success.

**The fallback warning is discarded.** `DescribeOptions` (`internal/template/describe.go:13`) has no `Stderr` field, so `FetchSource`'s stderr is `io.Discard` for both `template show` and the dashboard. That's why the version substitution was completely invisible — stderr was empty.

Minor: `intropy dashboard` has no `--registry-url` flag (env/config only), while `int message` does.

Want me to fix the silent-fallback pair — wire `Stderr` through `DescribeOptions` and make a non-tag ref either refuse or refresh rather than degrade quietly? That's separate from the U8 work, which is still uncommitted on top of the two gofmt fixes.

content.text:
Reproduced and diagnosed in the browser. Your `--template-version v0.9.0-beta.1` was right all along — that tag has the full manifest (message-ref **and** both derived annotations). Ignore my earlier suggestion of `v0.9.0`; the beta.1 tag you were already using is the better one.

## The cause: no registry is configured

Running your exact command, the API serves the field but with an empty pick list:

```
subscription   messageRef   suggestions=0   wiring=0
```

The frontend then renders it as a plain text box. Side by side, same field, same tag:

| | no registry (your run) | `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL` set |
|---|---|---|
| a11y node | `textbox` | `button … haspopup="listbox"` |
| options | — | `— none —`, `io.intropy.maxbo.catalog.product.updated`, `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export` |
| filter box | — | "Filter messages…" |

With the env var set, picking a message shows the derived routing exactly as designed:

> routes via `product-distribution-pubsub/sbt-test-product-extractor-001` · contract `ProductExport` (suggested)

Your `~/.intropy/config.yaml` has no `registryUrl` and no `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL` is exported. The registry itself is already running on :8787. So:

```
INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL=http://localhost:8787 i dashboard --template-version v0.9.0-beta.1
```

Better: add `registryUrl: http://localhost:8787` to the config, since `intropy dashboard` has no `--registry-url` flag (only `int message` does).

## A second, real bug: the field is buried

Even with the registry working, `subscription` is **inside the collapsed "advanced (5)" section** — you have to expand a disclosure to reach it. The partition in `web/src/components/useTemplateFields.ts:111` is:

```ts
() => inputs.filter((f) => f.required && !isResolved(f)),   // visible
() => inputs.filter((f) => !(f.required && !isResolved(f))), // advanced
```

`subscription` isn't `required` — the `anyOf` guard is what makes it mandatory — so it sorts into "advanced" alongside `idempotencyAppId`. The primary way to wire a loader is hidden behind a toggle, while `name` is the only thing on screen. That's almost certainly what made it look broken even when it wasn't.

## Suggested fix

Treat a message-ref field as visible regardless of `required` — it's the field the whole subscription flow exists for. One clause in that filter, plus the mirror in the `optional` filter. That pairs naturally with the CLI-side work I finished earlier, which made the same field the one thing an interactive `int create` asks about.

Want me to make that change? And separately, the two silent-fallback bugs from before (`Stderr` missing from `DescribeOptions`, branch refs degrading quietly) are still open — the U8 CLI work is also still uncommitted.

content.text:
Now I understand the pieces. There's one domain constraint worth stating before you choose, because it shapes the answer:

**A typed value can't silently be a subscription.** `form.tsx:45` is right that a message-ref is a *closed* reference — `int create` resolves it against the registry and rejects anything else (`unknown message reference: X / known messages: …`). So "write a name manually" can mean a message id the registry has but your cached list doesn't — fine — but it can't mean a *topic*, because the manual path is two different parameters (`topic` + `contract`).

That leaves a real fork in how to kill the toggle. Both fix the "buried under advanced" bug either way.

content.text:
Done, and verified in the browser. The toggle is gone; the value decides.

## What the drawer does now

On open, with nothing picked — no disclosure to expand:

```
* name         — Project name        [ OrderLoader                    ]
  subscription — Message subscription [ Select a message…           ▾ ]
  topic        — Topic                [ sbt-test-product-extractor-001 ]
  contract     — Contract type        [ ProductExport                  ]
  ▸ advanced (4)
```

Pick a message → `topic` and `contract` vanish and the routing appears:

> routes via `product-distribution-pubsub/sbt-test-product-extractor-001` · contract `ProductExport` (suggested)

Choose `— none —` → both come back, prefilled from workspace facts. Round trip verified in both directions.

Free text works as you asked. Typing something the catalog doesn't list offers a commit row and flags it:

```
Filter messages…  io.intropy.maxbo.order.placed
  use "io.intropy.maxbo.order.placed"        ← the only row
→ ! not in the registry catalog — create will reject
    this unless the registry declares it
```

That mirrors the CLI prompt, which also accepts a novel value and then fails naming the catalog — useful when the registry is stale, honest about what happens if it isn't.

## One thing I want to flag

I deliberately did **not** teach the form that "a message, or topic+contract" is the rule. `useTemplateFields.ts` already states the SPA never reimplements convention rules — the server computes them. So the Scaffold button now gates only on genuinely required fields (`name`), and if you clear all three wiring fields you'll get a server-side error rather than a disabled button. That error is the one I made legible in the earlier U8 work:

> the template requires either subscription, or topic and contract

If you'd rather the button gate on it client-side, say so — it's a few lines, but it does duplicate the schema's `anyOf` in the SPA.

## Changes

- `Combobox.tsx` — new `allowCustom` prop: a typed query that matches no option becomes a committable row, Enter prefers a filtered match over the typed text, and an off-list value still displays in the trigger.
- `useTemplateFields.ts` — `manualDerived`/`setManualDerived`/`derivedCount` deleted; `subscribed` (derived from the value) drives both the reveal and `submitValues` stripping. Message-ref and derived fields are exempt from the advanced split — that's the "buried under advanced" bug fixed.
- `CreateDrawer.tsx` — toggle block removed.
- `form.tsx` — `allowCustom` on the message combobox plus the uncatalogued warning.
- `index.css` — `.form-warning`, `.combo-option-custom`.

`make check` and `tsc --noEmit` pass. Test dashboards stopped; your registry on :8787 untouched.

Uncommitted now spans three separable commits — the two gofmt fixes, the U8 CLI prompt work, and this drawer change. Want me to commit them in that order? Still open from before: `--registry-url` missing on `dashboard`, and the silent template-version fallback.

content.text:
Confirmed no regression: with the registry set, the dropdown and its three options are there and the note is absent.

## What you were seeing

Not a new bug — the same missing registry. Your instance on 8730 reported `subscription: suggestions=None`, so the field fell through to a plain text box. The "dropdown with a pre-selected value" was `topic`: one workspace candidate makes it a `<datalist>` input, which Chrome draws with an arrow and prefills from your existing `product-loader`.

## What I fixed

The real defect was that this state was silent. A message field with no catalog now says so, right under the control:

> no message catalog — the dashboard has no message registry configured, or could not reach it. Set `registryUrl` in the config file (or `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL`) and reload to pick from the registry; a message id typed here still resolves at create.

Verified both states in the browser after a `make bundle`:

| | no registry | `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL` set |
|---|---|---|
| control | text box **+ the note** | dropdown, `— none —` + 2 messages |
| note | shown | absent |

Files: `web/src/components/form.tsx` (the `noCatalog` branch), `web/src/index.css` (`.form-note`). `make check` and `tsc --noEmit` pass.

## To see it working

```
INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL=http://localhost:8787 i dashboard --template-version v0.9.0-beta.1
```

You'll want to relaunch regardless to pick up the rebuilt binary. Worth putting `registryUrl: http://localhost:8787` in `~/.intropy/config.yaml` so you stop having to remember it — `intropy dashboard` still has no `--registry-url` flag, which is on the open list.

One note: nothing is listening on 8730 any more, only your 8731 instance. I don't think I stopped it — every `pkill` I ran required a literal `--port 880x`, which your portless command wouldn't match — but flagging it since I was killing processes nearby.

## Still uncommitted

Four separable commits now: the two gofmt fixes, the U8 CLI prompt work, the toggle removal + free-text combobox, and this no-catalog note. Want me to commit them in that order? Also open: `--registry-url` on `dashboard`, and the silent `--template-version` fallback (a branch ref resolves to a cached tag with no warning, because `DescribeOptions` has no `Stderr`).
